questions.q: If $\int \frac{a \cos x-2 \sin x}{b \sin x+5 \cos x} d x=\frac{7}{41} x+\frac{22}{7} \log|b \sin x+5 \cos x|+C,(a>0, b>0)$, then $\int \frac{d x}{b+a \cos x}=$
questions.solution: We have, $\int \frac{a \cos x-2 \sin x}{b \sin x+5 \cos x} d x=\frac{7}{41} x+\frac{22}{41}\begin{aligned} & \log |(b \sin x+5 \cos x)|+C \\ & \text { Now, let } a \cos x-2 \sin x=\lambda(b \sin x+5 \cos x) \\ & \qquad+\mu(b \cos x-5 \sin x)\end{aligned}\therefore a=5 \lambda+\mu b$ and $-2=b \lambda-5 \mu$ But it is given, $\lambda=\frac{7}{41}$ and $\mu=\frac{22}{41}a=3, b=4\int \frac{d x}{b+a \cos x}=\int \frac{d x}{4+3 \cos x}=\int \frac{\left(1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right) d x}{4\left(1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)+3\left(1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)}\begin{aligned} &=\int \frac{\sec ^2 x / 2}{7+\tan ^2 x / 2} d x \\ & \tan \frac{x}{2}=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x=2 d t \\ & \frac{d x}{b+a \cos x}=2 \int \frac{d t}{7+t^2} \\ &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{t}{\sqrt{7}}+C \\ &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan x / 2}{\sqrt{7}}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{\text{3 sin x + 2 cos x}}{\text{3 cos x + 2 sin x}} \text{dx = ax + b} \text\ln \left|\text{2 sin x + 3 cos x}\right| + \text{C}$, then
questions.solution:
Differentiating both sides, we get

$~\dfrac{\text{3 sin x + 2 cos x}}{\text{3 cos x + 2 sin x}} = = \text{a} + \dfrac{\text{b(2 cos x - 3 sin x)}}{\text{(2 sin x + 3 cos x)}}$

$= \dfrac{\text{sin x (2a - 3b) + cos x (3a + 2b)}}{\left(\text{3 cos x + 2 sin x}\right)}$

Comparing like terms on both sides, we get

$3 = 2 \text{a} - 3 \text{b, 2 = 3a + 2b} \to \text{a} = \dfrac{1 2}{1 3} \text{, b =} - \dfrac{1 5}{3 9}$

questions.q: $∫ e^{x}\left[\dfrac{2 + sin ⁡ 2x}{1 + cos ⁡ 2x}\right]dx =$
questions.solution:
Let,& $I = ∫ e^{x}\left[\dfrac{2 + sin ⁡ 2x}{1 + cos ⁡ 2x}\right]dx$

We know that~$sin2x = 2sinxcosx \text{ and } cos2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1$

Using the above formulas we can write

$I = ∫ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{2 + 2sinxcosx}{2\cos^{2}x}\right)dx$

$I = ∫ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{2\left(1 + sinxcosx\right)}{2\cos^{2}x}\right)dx$

$I = ∫ e^{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x} + \dfrac{sinxcosx}{\cos^{2}x}\right)dx$
$I = ∫ e^{x} ( tanx + \sec^{2} x )dx$

We know that~$∫ e^{x}\left(\text{f}\left(\text{x}\right) + f^{'}\left(\text{x}\right)\right)\text{dx} = e^{x} \cdot \text{f} + \text{C}$

Using the above formula we can write

$I = e^{x} tanx + C$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text { If } \frac{4 x^2+5 x^4+7}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+1} \\ & +\frac{C x^3+D x^2+E x+F}{x^4+x^2+1}, \text { then } \\ & B+2(D+F+E)-C \cdot A=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution: We have, $\begin{aligned} & \frac{4 x^2+5 x^4+7}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+1}+\frac{C x^3+D x^2+E x+F}{x^4+x^2+1} \\ & \Rightarrow 4 x^2+5 x^4+7=(A x+B)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right) \\ & +\left(C x^3+D x^2+E x+F\right)\left(x^2+1\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 5 x^4+4 x^2+7=A x^5+A x^3+A x+B x^4+B x^2 \\ & +B+C x^5+C x^3+D x^4+D x^2+E x^3+E x+F x^2+F \\ & \Rightarrow 5 x^4+4 x^2+7=(A+C) x^5+(B+D) x^4 \\ & +(A+C+E) x^3+(B+D+F) x^2+(A+E) x+(B+F) \\ \end{aligned}$ On comparing, we get $\begin{aligned} & A+C=0 \\ & B+D=5 \end{aligned}\begin{array}{r} A+C+E=0 \\ B+D+F=4 \\ A+E=0 \\ B+F=7 \end{array} On solving, we get \begin{gathered}$A=C=E=0, B=8 . D=-3, F=-1 \\ \therefore B+2(D+F+E)-C $\cdot$A=8+2(-3-1+0)-0 $\times$0 \\ =8-8=0 \end{gathered}

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{1}{( x - 2{)}^{5} ( x - 1{)}^{4}}dx = \mathop{∑}_{r = - 4}^{- 1}{A}_{r}\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)r + \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{3}{A}_{r}\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)r + Bf\left(x\right),$~then $f\left(x\right) =$
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(x - 2\right)5 . \left(x - 1\right)4}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(x - 2\right)9 . \left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)4}$

Let $\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2} = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x - 2\right) . 1 - \left(x - 1\right) . 1}{ \left(x - 2\right)2}dx = dt$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 1}{\left(x - 2\right)2}$dx = dt . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, \dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2} =$t$

$⇒ x - 1 = tx - 2t$

$⇒ x = $\dfrac{2t - 1}{t - 1}

$⇒ x - 2 = $\dfrac{1}{t - 1} . . . \left(2\right)$

$∴ I = ∫ $\dfrac{- dt}{\dfrac{1}{\left(t - 1\right)7}}$t^{4}$

$⇒ I = ∫ $\dfrac{\left(1 - t\right)7}{t4}$dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ $\dfrac{1 - c1 7 t + c2 7 t^{2} - c3 7 t^{3} + . . . . . . + c6 7 . t^{6} - c7 7 t^{7}}{t4}$dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ $\dfrac{1}{t4}$dt - c1 7 ∫ $\dfrac{dt}{t3} +$c2 7 ∫ $\dfrac{dt}{t2} -$c3 7 ∫ $\dfrac{1}{t}$dt + . . . . - c7 7 ∫ t^{3}dt$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{t- 4 + 1}{- 4 + 1} -7\dfrac{t- 3 + 1}{- 3 + 1} +$c2 7 $\dfrac{t- 2 + 1}{- 2 + 1} -$c3 7 log\left|t\right| + . . . - $\dfrac{t4}{4} +$c$

~ $⇒ I = $\dfrac{- 1}{3}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)-$3 + $\dfrac{7}{2}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)-$2 - c3 7 log \left|$\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right| + . . . . . - \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)$4 + c$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{- 1}{3} \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)$3 + $\dfrac{7}{2} \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)$2 + c2 7 \$left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right) +$c4 7 \$left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)-$1 + c3 7 \left[log\left(x - 2\right) - log \left($x - 1\right)\right] . . . . - $\dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)-4 + c . . . \left(1\right)$

$∵$Given that

$∫ \dfrac{1}{( x - 2{)}^{5} ( x - 1{)}^{4}}dx = \mathop{∑}_{r = - 4}^{- 1}{A}_{r} $\$left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)r + \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{3}{A}_{r} $\$left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)$r + Bf \left(x\right)$

$∴$We get $f \left($x\right) = log \left($x - 2\right) - $log\left($x - 1\right)$

questions.q: If $∫ f  \left(x\right)cos ⁡ xdx = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left\{f\left($x\right)\right\}$2 + c,$ then f\left($x\right)$ is$
questions.solution:
Given,& $∫ f\left(x\right)cos ⁡ xdx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{f\left(x\right)\right\}2 + c$

Differentiate both sides we get,~

$f\left(x\right)cos ⁡ x = \dfrac{1}{2} ⋅ 2f\left(x\right)f^{′} ( x )$

Then, $f^{′}\left(x\right) = cos ⁡ x$

Integrate both the sides we get,~

$f\left(x\right) = sin ⁡ x + c$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x^4} \mathrm{~d} x=\mathrm{A}(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)^{\mathrm{m}}+\mathrm{c}$ for a suitable chosen integer $\mathrm{m}$ and a function $\mathrm{A}(x)$, where $\mathrm{c}$ is a constant of integration, then $(\mathrm{A}(x))^{\mathrm{m}}$ equals
questions.solution: $\text { Let } \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}$& =$\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x^4} \mathrm{~d}$x \\ & =$\int \frac{x \sqrt{\frac{1}{x^2}-1}}{x^4} \mathrm{~d}$x \\ & =$\int \frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{x^2}-1}}{x^3} \mathrm{~d}$x \end{aligned} Let $\frac{1}{x^2}-1=\mathrm{t}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad\frac{-2}{x^3}$& $\mathrm{~d}$x=$\mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x^3} \mathrm{~d}$x=$\frac{-\mathrm{dt}}{2}$\\ \therefore \quad $\mathrm{I}$& =-$\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}$\\ & =$\frac{-1}{2} \times \frac{(\mathrm{t})^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}+\mathrm{c}$\\ & =$\frac{-1}{3} \times\left(\frac{1}{x^2}-$1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+$\mathrm{c}$\\ & =$\frac{-1}{3} \times \frac{\left(1-x^2\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(x^2\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}+\mathrm{c}$\\ & =$\frac{-1}{3} \times \frac{\left(\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)^3}{x^3} \end{aligned}$Comparing with $\mathrm{A}(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)^{\mathrm{m}}+\mathrm{c}$, we get $\begin{gathered} \mathrm{A}($x)=$\frac{-1}{3 x^3} \text { and } \mathrm{m}=$3 \\ \therefore \quad($\mathrm{A}($x))^{\mathrm{m}}=\left(\frac{-1}{3 x^3}\right)^3=$\frac{-1}{27 x^9} \end{gathered}$

questions.q: The value of $\int e^{x}\left[\frac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right] d x$ is
questions.solution: Let $I=\int e^{x}\left[\frac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right] d x\begin{aligned}=& \int\left\{\frac{e^{x}}{(1+\cos x)}+\frac{e^{x} \sin x}{(1+\cos x)}\right\} d x \\=& \int \frac{e^{x}}{2 \cos ^{2} \frac{x}{2}} d x+\int \frac{e^{x} \cdot 2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{x}{2}}{2 \cos ^{2} \frac{x}{2}} \cdot d x \\=& \frac{1}{2} \int e^{x} \cdot \sec ^{2} \frac{x}{2} \cdot d x+\int \underset{\mathbb{I}}{e^{x} \tan } \frac{x}{2} \cdot d x \\=& \frac{1}{2} \int e^{x} \cdot \sec ^{2} \frac{x}{2} \cdot d x \\+\left\{\tan \frac{x}{2} \cdot e^{x}-\int \frac{1}{2} \cdot \sec ^{2} \frac{x}{2} \cdot e^{x} d x\right\} \end{aligned}$ (using integral by parts) $=\frac{1}{2} \int e^{x} \cdot \sec ^{2} \frac{x}{2} d x+e^{x} \cdot \tan \frac{x}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int e^{x} \cdot \sec ^{2} \frac{x}{2} \cdot d x=e^{x} \cdot \tan \frac{x}{2}+C$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{x^3 \mathrm{~d} x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}=\mathrm{a}\left(1+x^2\right) \sqrt{1+x^2}+\mathrm{b} \sqrt{1+x^2}+\mathrm{c}$ (where $\mathrm{c}$ is a constant of integration), then the value of $3 \mathrm{ab}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Put } 1+x^2=\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x \mathrm{~d} x=2 \mathrm{t} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \Rightarrow x \mathrm{~d} x=\mathrm{t} d \mathrm{t} \\ & \quad \int \frac{x^3 \mathrm{~d} x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}} \\ & =\int \frac{\mathrm{t}^2-1}{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{t} d \mathrm{t} \\ & =\int\left(\mathrm{t}^2-1\right) \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{t}^3}{3}-\mathrm{t}+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{\left(1+x^2\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}-\sqrt{1+x^2}+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{1}{3}\left(1+x^2\right) \sqrt{1+x^2}-\sqrt{1+x^2}+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad & a=\frac{1}{3}, b=-1 \\ & \Rightarrow 3 a b=-1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^4}}{x^7} d x=f(x)\left\{\sqrt{1-x^4}\right\}^n+C$, then $(f(x))^n$ is equal to
questions.solution: $I=\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^4}}{x^7} d x$ Let $x^2=u$, then $2 x d x=d u$ I=$\int \frac{\sqrt{1-u^2}}{2 u^4}$d u=$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sqrt{1-u^2}}{u^4}$d u Let $u=\sin v$, then $d u=\cos v d v\begin{aligned}$I & =$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\cos ^2 v}{\sin ^4 v}$d v=$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{\cos ^2 v \tan ^4 v}$d v \\ & =$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sec ^2 v}{\tan ^4 v}$d v \end{aligned} Let $\tan v=w$, then $\sec ^2 v d v=d w\begin{aligned}$& \quad I=$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d w}{w^4}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{w^{-3}}{-3}\right)=\frac{-1}{6 w^3}+$C \\ & =$\frac{-1}{6 \tan ^3 v}=\frac{-\left(\sqrt{1-u^2}\right)^3}{6 u^3}=-\frac{1}{6} \frac{\left(1-x^4\right)^{3 / 2}}{x^6}+$C \\ & \therefore \quad I=$\frac{-1}{6} \frac{\left(1-x^4\right)^{3 / 2}}{x^6}+$C \end{aligned} Now, $I=f(x)\left(1-x^4\right)^{n / 2}+C$ on Comparing, we obtain $\begin{gathered}$f(x)=$\frac{-1}{6 x^6} \text { and }$n=3 \\ \therefore \quad(f(x))^n=\left(-\frac{1}{6 x^6}\right)^3=$\frac{-1}{216 x^{18}} \end{gathered}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{3-x^2}{1-2 x+x^2} e^x d x=e^x f(x)+c \Rightarrow f(x)$
questions.solution:
Let $\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{3-x^2}{1-2 x+x^2} e^x d x \\ & =\int \frac{3-x^2}{(1-x)^2} e^x d x \\ & =\int\left(\frac{2}{(1-x)^2}+\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right) e^x d x\end{aligned}$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{aligned}$& e^x\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)+$c=e^x f(x)+c \\ & \Rightarrow \quad f(x)=$\frac{1+x}{1-x}$\\ & \end{aligned} $

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sin x}{\cos x(1+\cos x)} d x=f(x)+c$, then $f(x)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\text { Let } I=\int \frac{\sin x}{\cos x(1+\cos x)} d x$
Put $\cos x=t \Rightarrow-\sin x d x=d t\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad I & =\int \frac{-d t}{t(1+t)} \\
& =-\int\left[\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{(1+t)}\right] d t \\
& =-[\log t-\log (1+t)]+c \\
& =\log \left(\frac{t+1}{t}\right)+c
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text { But } I=\int(x)+c \\
& \therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{\cos x+1}{\cos x}\right)+c=f(x)+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f(x)=\log \left(\frac{1+\cos x}{\cos x}\right)
\end{aligned}$

Let $x^{50}=t \Rightarrow 50 x^{49} d x=d t\therefore \quad I=\frac{1}{50} \int \frac{\tan ^{-1} t}{1+t^2} d t$
Let $\tan ^{-1} t=u \Rightarrow \frac{1}{1+t^2} d t=d u\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad I & =\frac{1}{50} \int u d u=\frac{u^2}{100}+c \\
& =\frac{\left(\tan ^{-1} x^{50}\right)^2}{100}+c
\end{aligned}$
But $I=k\left(\tan ^{-1} x^{50}\right)^2+c$(given)
$\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow& k\left(\tan ^{-1}x^{50}\right)^2+c & =\frac{1}{100}\left(\tan ^{-1}x^{50}\right)^2+c \\ \Rightarrow & & k & =\frac{1}{100}\end{array}$

questions.q: $\int e^{\tan x}\left(\sec ^{2} x+\sec ^{3} x \sin x\right) d x$ is equal to
questions.solution: Let $I=\int e^{\tan x}\left(\sec ^{2} x+\sec ^{3} x \sin x\right) d x=\int e^{\tan x}(1+\tan x) \sec ^{2} x d x$ Put $\tan x=t\Rightarrow \sec ^{2} x d x=d tI=\int e^{t}(1+t) d t=e^{t}+\int t e^{t} d t=e^{t}+t e^{t}-e^{t}+c=t e^{t}+c=\tan x e^{\tan x}+c$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x}(x+9)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let
$I=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x}(x+9)}$
Put
$\begin{aligned} x & =t^2 \Rightarrow d x=2 t d t \\ & =\int \frac{2 t d t}{t\left(t^2+9\right)}=2 \cdot \frac{1}{3} \tan ^{-1} \frac{t}{3}+C \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{3}+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{a^2 \sin ^2 x+b^2 \cos ^2 x}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{d x}{a^2 \sin ^2 x+b^2 \cos ^2 x} \\ & =\frac{1}{a^2} \int \frac{\sec ^2 x d x}{\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^2+\tan ^2 x} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad=\frac{1}{a b} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a \tan x}{b}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{I}=\int \sin (\log (x)) \mathrm{d} x$, then $\mathrm{I}$ is given by
options: $-\frac{x}{2}(\sin (\log x)-\cos (\log x))+\mathrm{c}$, where $\mathrm{c}$ is a constant of integration.
$\frac{x}{2}(\sin (\log x)-\cos (\log x))+\mathrm{c}, \text { where } \mathrm{c}$ is a constant of integration.
$\frac{x}{2}(\sin (\log x)+\cos (\log x))+\mathrm{c}$, where $\mathrm{c}$ is a constant of 'integration.
$-\frac{x}{2}(\sin (\log x)+\cos (\log x))+\mathrm{c}$, where c is a constant of integration.
questions.solution: Let $\log x=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow x=\mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}$ Differentiating w.r.t. t, we get $\mathrm{d}x=\mathrme^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \mathrm{I}& =\int \sin (\mathrm{t}) \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}\\ & =\sin \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}-\int \cos \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}\\ & =\sin \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}- \left[\cos \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}+\int \sin \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}\right]\\ & =\sin \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}-\cos \mathrm{t} \mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{I} \end{aligned}\begin{array}{ll}\therefore& 2 \mathrm{I}=x \sin (\log x)-x \cos (\log x)+$\mathrm{c}$\\ \therefore \quad \text{ and } $\mathrm{I}=\frac{x}{2}(\sin (\logx)-\cos (\logx))+ \mathrm{c}\end{array}

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{1-\cos x-\sin x}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $\begin{aligned}$I & =$\int \frac{d x}{1-\cos x-\sin x}$\\
& =$\int \frac{d x}{1-\left(\frac{1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}\right)-\frac{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}{1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}}$\\
& =$\int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x}{1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}-1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}-2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}
\end{aligned} =\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x}{\tan \frac{x}{2}\left(\tan \frac{x}{2}-1\right)}$Let $\tan \frac{x}{2}=z\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{2} \sec ^2 $\frac{x}{2}$d x=d z \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sec ^2 $\frac{x}{2}$d x=2 d z \\
& \therefore $I=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 d z}{z(z-1)}=\int  \left(\frac{1}{z-1}-\frac{1}{z}\right)$d z \\
& \quad=\log (z-1)-\log z+C \\
& =\log $\$left(\frac{z-1}{z}\right)+C=\log \left[\frac{\tan \frac{x}{2}-1}{\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right]+$C \\
& \quad=\log \left[$1-\cot $\frac{x}{2}\right]+$C
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \sec ^2 x \operatorname{cosec}^4 x d x=-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+k \tan x-2 \cot x+C$, then $k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \sec ^2 x \operatorname{cosec}^4 x d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{1}{\sin ^4 x \cos ^2 x} d x=\int \frac{\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x}{\sin ^4 x \cos ^2 x} d x \\ & =\int \frac{d x}{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}+\int \frac{d x}{\sin ^4 x} \\ & \left.=\int \frac{\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) d x}{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}+\int \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\right) \\ & =\int\left(\sec ^2 x+\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\right) d x \\ & \quad+\int \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\left(1+\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) \\ & =\tan x-\cot x+\int \operatorname{cosec}{ }^2 x d x \\ & =\tan x-\cot x-\cot x-\frac{\cot ^3 x}{3}+C \\ & =-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+\tan x-2 \cot ^2 x+C \cot ^2 x d x\end{aligned}$
But it given that,
$\begin{aligned} & I=-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+k \tan x-2 \cot x+C \\ \therefore \quad k & =1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{\sin x \cdot \sec ^2 x-\tan x \cdot \sin x+\cos x}{(1-\cos 2 x)} d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned}$& $\text {Take } \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\sin x \sec ^2 x-\tan x \cdot \sin x+\cos x}{(1-\cos 2 x)} \cdot$d x \\ & $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\sin x \sec ^2 x-\tan x \cdot \sin x+\cos x}{1-1+2 \sin ^2 x} \cdot$d x \\ & $\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\int \frac{\sec ^2 x}{\sin x} \cdot$d x-$\int \sec$x d x+$\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin ^2 x} \cdot$d x\right] \\ & $\text { Let } \sin$x=t \\ & \cos x d x=d t \\ & $\$mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} $\$left[\int \frac{1+\tan ^2 x}{\sin x} \cdotdx-\log |\sec x+\tan x|+\int \frac{d t}{t^2}\right]\\ \text{ and } \$mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\int \operatorname{cosec}$x d $x+\int \secx \tan$x+d x-\log |\sec x+\tan x|$-\frac{1}{t}\right]+$c \\ \text{ and } \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}[\log |\operatorname{cosec}x-\cot x|+\sec x-\operatorname{cosec} x-\log |\sec x+\tan x|] \\ \text{ and } I=\frac{1}{2}\left[\secx-\operatorname{cosec}x+\log \left|\frac{2 \cos 2 x / 2}{2 \sin ^{x / 2} \cos ^{x / 2}}\right|-\log \left|\frac{\cos ^{x / 2}+\sin ^{x / 2}}{\cos ^{x / 2}-\sin ^{x / 2}}\right|\right]$\\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\secx-\operatorname{cosec}x+\log  \left|\tan $\frac{x}{2}\right|-\log \left|\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{x}{2}\right)\right|\right]$\\ \text{ and } \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\secx-\operatorname{cosec}x-\log \left|\frac{\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{x}{2}\right)}{\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right|\right]+c \text {. }\\ \text{ and } \end{aligned} So, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: If $\int \frac{(x-1) d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}}=A \cdot \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{f(x)}+$ constant, then the ordered pair $(A, f(-1))=$
questions.solution: We have, $\int \frac{(x-1) d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}}=A \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{f(x)}+C$ Let $\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{(x-1) d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} \\ & =\int \frac{x-1}{x(x+1) \sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}} d x \end{aligned}$ Put, $\begin{aligned} x+\frac{1}{x}+1 & =t \text { and }\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) d x=d t \\ & =\int \frac{(x-1)}{x(x+1) \sqrt{t}} \times \frac{x^2}{\left(x^2-1\right)} d t \\ & =\int \frac{x}{(x+1)^2 \sqrt{t}} d t=\int \frac{d t}{\frac{x^2+2 x+1}{t}} \\ & =\int \frac{d t}{\left(1+x+\frac{1}{x}+1\right) \sqrt{t}}=\int \frac{d t}{(1+t) \sqrt{t}} \\ = & 2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{t}+C=2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}+C \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad A=2 \Rightarrow f(x)=x+\frac{1}{x}+1 \\ & A=2 \Rightarrow f(-1)=-1-1+1=-1 \\ & \therefore \quad(A, f(-1)=(2,-1) \\ & \end{aligned}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x-x^2}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x-x^2}} \\ & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \times \frac{d x}{\sqrt{1-x}}\end{aligned}$
Put $\quad \sqrt{x}=\sin \theta\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}} d x & =\cos \theta d \theta \\ \therefore \quad I & =\int \frac{2 \cos \theta d \theta}{\sqrt{1-\sin ^2 \theta}} \\ & =\int \frac{2 \cos \theta}{\cos \theta} d \theta \\ & =\int 2 d \theta=2 \theta+C \\ & =2 \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{x}+C\end{aligned}$
